from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Meet the complex plane: real and imaginary axes.", "Think of complex numbers as vectors.", "A point like 3+4i defines a position."]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Complex Plane", lecture_lines)
        
        # 1. Fade in the complex plane with labeled real/imaginary axes
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[-1, 6, 1],
            y_range=[-1, 6, 1],
            axis_config={"color": WHITE}
        )
        real_label = Text("Real", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(axes.x_axis.get_end(), RIGHT)
        imag_label = Text("Imaginary", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(axes.y_axis.get_end(), UP)
        plane = VGroup(axes, real_label, imag_label)
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(Write(plane))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # 2. Plot a point z = x + iy on the complex plane
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        point_z = Dot(axes.c2p(3, 4), color="#00FF00")
        label_z = MathTex("z = 3+4i", font_size=24, color="#00FF00").next_to(point_z, UR)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(point_z), Write(label_z))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")

        # 3. Draw a vector from the origin to z
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        vec = Arrow(start=axes.c2p(0, 0), end=axes.c2p(3, 4), buff=0, color="#FF0000")
        
        self.play(Create(vec))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF0000")
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Multiplying by i rotates 90 degrees.", "e^(iθ) represents continuous rotation.", "Moving along the unit circle."]
        self.setup_layout("Rotational Motion and the Exponential Function", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        circle = Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'C3')
        point = Dot(color=YELLOW).move_to(circle.point_at_angle(0))
        angle_text = MathTex(r"\theta", color=PURPLE)
        self.place_at_grid(angle_text, 'E5')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW), Create(circle))
        self.add(point)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(PURPLE))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        
        # Animate continuous rotation
        angle_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        
        def update_point(mob):
            angle = angle_tracker.get_value()
            mob.move_to(circle.point_at_angle(angle))
            
        point.add_updater(update_point)
        
        self.play(angle_tracker.animate.set_value(2 * PI), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        point.remove_updater(update_point)
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Euler's formula: e^(iθ) = cos(θ) + i sin(θ).",
            "Angle θ sweeps an arc on the circle.",
            "Tracing coordinates as cos and sin.",
            "Input θ links circles to exponentials.",
            "Observe the circle's rotation."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Euler’s Formula: Linking Circles and Exponentials", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        formula = MathTex("e^{i\\theta} = \\cos(\\theta) + i \\sin(\\theta)", font_size=40)
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'A2', 'B5')
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1.5, 1.5], y_range=[-1.5, 1.5], x_length=3, y_length=3).scale(0.8)
        circle = Circle(radius=axes.c2p(1,0)[0] - axes.c2p(0,0)[0], color=WHITE)
        circle.move_to(axes.c2p(0,0))
        self.place_at_grid(axes, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'D3', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(circle))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        theta = ValueTracker(0)
        dot = Dot(color="#FF0000")
        
        def update_dot(d):
            angle = theta.get_value()
            d.move_to(axes.c2p(np.cos(angle), np.sin(angle)))
        
        dot.add_updater(update_dot)
        self.add(dot)
        
        self.play(theta.animate.set_value(2 * PI), run_time=3, rate_func=linear)
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        rect = SurroundingRectangle(formula, color=BLUE)
        self.play(Create(rect))
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(BLUE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        final_text = Text("Rotation completed!", color=YELLOW, font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(final_text, 'F3')
        self.play(FadeIn(final_text))
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Grand Finale: Deriving e^(πi) = -1", [
            "Set θ to π.",
            "cos(π) is -1 and sin(π) is 0.",
            "Plugging into Euler’s formula.",
            "The point hits (-1, 0).",
            "Resulting in e^(πi) = -1."
        ])
        
        # Initial Formula
        euler_formula = MathTex("e^{i\\theta} = \\cos\\theta + i\\sin\\theta", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(euler_formula, 'B2')
        self.play(Write(euler_formula))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Set θ to π.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        theta_pi = MathTex("e^{i\\pi} = \\cos\\pi + i\\sin\\pi", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(theta_pi, 'B2')
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(euler_formula, theta_pi))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # cos(π) is -1 and sin(π) is 0.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Plugging into Euler’s formula.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        plugged_formula = MathTex("e^{i\\pi} = -1 + i(0)", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(plugged_formula, 'C3')
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(theta_pi, plugged_formula))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # The point hits (-1, 0).
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        axes = ComplexPlane(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], axis_config={"include_numbers": True}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(axes, 'E3')
        point = Dot(axes.c2p(-1, 0), color=RED)
        label = MathTex("(-1, 0)", font_size=24).next_to(point, UP)
        self.play(Create(axes), FadeIn(point), Write(label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Resulting in e^(πi) = -1.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF4500"))
        final_result = MathTex("e^{i\\pi} = -1", font_size=48, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(final_result, 'E5')
        self.play(Write(final_result), Indicate(final_result))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis and Beauty", ["Connecting five constants: e, i, π, 1, 0.", "They form one elegant equation.", "Euler's identity remains beautiful."])
        
        # Define the constants as colored objects
        constants = VGroup(
            MathTex("e", color="#FF5733"),
            MathTex("i", color="#33FF57"),
            MathTex("\\pi", color="#3357FF"),
            MathTex("1", color="#F3FF33"),
            MathTex("0", color="#FF33F3")
        )
        
        # Position them initially
        self.place_at_grid(constants[0], "B2", scale_factor=2.0)
        self.place_at_grid(constants[1], "B4", scale_factor=2.0)
        self.place_at_grid(constants[2], "D2", scale_factor=2.0)
        self.place_at_grid(constants[3], "D4", scale_factor=2.0)
        self.place_at_grid(constants[4], "E3", scale_factor=2.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(FadeIn(constants))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        equation = MathTex("e^{i\\pi} + 1 = 0", font_size=60)
        self.place_in_area(equation, "B2", "E4")
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(constants),
            Write(equation)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(self.camera.frame.animate.set_width(16))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Unveiling Euler's Identity: The Most Beautiful Equation
outline.target_audience: High school students with basic trigonometry and complex number knowledge

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Complex Plane
sections.content: Introduce the complex plane where the horizontal axis represents real numbers and the vertical axis represents imaginary numbers (i). Visualize a point as a vector.
sections.example: Represent the number 3 + 4i as an arrow starting at (0,0) and pointing to the coordinate (3,4) on a grid.

sections.title: Rotational Motion and the Exponential Function
sections.content: Explain that multiplying by 'i' is equivalent to a 90-degree counter-clockwise rotation. Introduce the idea that e^(iθ) represents a continuous rotation along the unit circle.
sections.example: Imagine a tiny 'math-bot' starting at (1,0); multiplying its position by i repeatedly makes it jump 90 degrees around the circle.

sections.title: Euler’s Formula: Linking Circles and Exponentials
sections.content: Introduce Euler's formula: e^(iθ) = cos(θ) + i sin(θ). Visually demonstrate how the input θ sweeps an arc on the unit circle, resulting in coordinates (cos θ, sin θ).
sections.example: A clock hand spinning: as the angle θ increases, the tip of the clock hand traces the circumference of a circle with radius 1.

sections.title: The Grand Finale: Deriving e^(πi) = -1
sections.content: Set θ = π. Show that cos(π) = -1 and sin(π) = 0. Plug these into the formula to show the result hits the point (-1, 0) on the complex plane.
sections.example: Our 'math-bot' from section 2 rotates exactly 180 degrees (π radians) from (1,0) to land perfectly on the real axis at -1.

sections.title: Synthesis and Beauty
sections.content: Conclude by highlighting why this formula is famous: it connects the five most important mathematical constants (e, i, π, 1, 0) in one elegant, simple statement.
sections.example: Display the five constants as puzzle pieces clicking together to form the 'bridge' that is Euler's Identity.
